market_summary: The pre-market setup is mixed and wait-and-see, based on 1560 articles from Yahoo Finance, TradingView, Reuters, CNBC Markets, Seeking Alpha. The dominant theme is macro, with 745 macro items, 426 company items, 330 industry items, and 59 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.
macro_summary: Late Cycle Markets are balancing easier policy expectations against growth and earnings risk, keeping leadership narrow and confirmation dependent. The market is taking its direction from Fed/rates, with investors testing whether policy support can offset slower growth and earnings risk. Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (180), inflation (135), oil/energy (107), growth/jobs (21). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_summary: Sentiment is mixed and wait-and-see: 180 positive, 195 negative, and 1185 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.
